related.note: The same magnesium-bismuth piece in Nolan's Stanford lab, but this telling attributes it to Ubatuba, Brazil, where the story says it came from Roswell.

plain: A fisherman on a beach at Ubatuba, Brazil, is said to have watched an object explode, in 1957 by one account, and fragments of it later ended up in the Stanford laboratory of the scientist Garry Nolan, who studied them with mass spectrometry, a lab method that shows what a material is made of. Michels tells this himself across several episodes, saying the pieces were first mailed to the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée, that Nolan spoke about them on Joe Rogan's podcast, and in one episode that Nolan holds "this magnesium bismuth piece," a sample made of those two metals. Michels raises it as physical material that a working scientist can test, though in some tellings he gives the date and in others he does not, and only one mentions the metals.
